neighbours.label: the period ending the results of a structured abstract, just before 'Conclusion'
fire:
Background. We studied 40 patients. Methods. Each one had surgery. Results. No infection occurred in the treated group.
Conclusion. This method is safe.
Methods: A chart review of 200 cases. Results: Mean age was 61 and survival was 80% (P = .03). CONCLUSIONS: Survival improved over time.

Objective. To test the vaccine. Results. Antibody levels were higher at week 8 (p=0.012).
Conclusions. The vaccine is effective.

Aim: To map the wetlands. Results: Coverage for ducks was good under current conditions.
Conclusion: Managers can rely on these maps.
Background: Few data exist. Results: Tumours of this type were extremely rare. Conclusion: A larger study is needed.

Methods. We measured blood pressure. Results. Age had no influence on the outcome (p=0.51).
Conclusion. Age is not a risk factor.
Purpose: To compare two drugs. Results: Rates were 12 and 19 per year (P = .22). CONCLUSIONS: The drugs did not differ.

Objective. To test new sensors. Results. Sensitivity improved by 30% in the magnetic field tests.
Conclusion. These sensors are ready.
quiet:
We met 40 patients at the clinic. Each one had a story. Nobody was in a hurry that day.
Later we all went home.
The office keeps a file of 200 cases. Most are from the 1980s and the rest are newer. The boxes are in the basement.

The vaccine arrived on Monday. Staff put it in the fridge at the back.
The nurses came in on Tuesday.

We walked around the wetlands. There were many ducks that day and the weather was good.
The managers gave us coffee.
Few people live here. Winters in this valley are extremely cold. A larger town lies to the south.

We measured the room with a tape. It was smaller than we had thought.
The sofa did not fit.
Two shops sell these drugs. One is open 12 hours a day and the other 19. Both close on Sunday.

New sensors arrived this week. They are small and come in a box.
We will fit them in spring.
